title: Dark Energy
objective: After this level you can explain the discovery that the universe’s expansion is speeding up.
summary: In 1998, distant supernovae showed that the expansion is speeding up. Its unknown cause, dark energy, is about 68% of the universe.

cards.headline: The universe’s expansion is speeding up, and no one knows why.
cards.body: Everyone expected the opposite. Then, in 1998, the universe turned out to have its foot on the gas.

cards.headline: Expecting a slowdown
cards.body: Toss a ball upward and gravity slows it down. Gravity pulls everything together, so astronomers expected the expansion of the universe to be slowing the same way. In 1998 two teams checked, using distant supernovae. The supernovae were fainter than a slowing universe allowed. The expansion is speeding up. The ball wasn’t slowing down. It was taking off.

cards.headline: Dark energy
cards.body: Whatever is pressing the accelerator has a name, dark energy, and that’s about all we have: nobody knows what it is. Don’t mix it up with dark matter, which adds gravity. Dark energy speeds up the expansion. Yet dark energy makes up roughly 68% of the universe’s energy content, and dark matter about 27%. Everything made of ordinary atoms, every star, planet and person, is only about 5%. We’re the sprinkles on a very mysterious cake.

mascot.line: Dark matter and dark energy share a word, not a job. Level 85's dark matter adds gravity; this one speeds up the expansion.

cards.fact: The discovery won the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics.
cards.context: Saul Perlmutter, Brian Schmidt and Adam Riess shared it for discovering the accelerating expansion. Not bad for finding the exact opposite of what everyone expected.

questions.explanation: Distant supernovae were fainter than expected: the expansion is accelerating.

questions.prompt: Roughly how much of the universe is ordinary matter, the stuff of stars, planets and people?
questions.explanation: Ordinary matter is only about 5%. Dark matter is about 27% and dark energy about 68%.

questions.prompt: From Level 85: how are dark matter and dark energy different?

options.label: They are two names for the same thing
Dark matter glows faintly; dark energy doesn’t
Dark matter adds gravity; dark energy speeds up expansion
Dark energy is made of black holes

questions.explanation: Dark matter’s gravity holds galaxies together; dark energy drives the expansion to accelerate.
